description: 1 drawing : ink brush, blue watercolor, and opaque white over graphite underdrawing ; 21.7 x 31.7 cm (sheet) | Editorial cartoon shows United States Secretary of State John Foster Dulles in front of a huge auditorium, divided into two sections, one labeled "Friends" and the other "Influenced People."  Only two sit on the Friends side:  German Chancellor Konrad Adenauer, dressed as a schoolboy labeled "Star Pupil," and British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan, shown as a poodle labeled "Old Faithful."  The Influenced People section is empty with overturned and broken chairs labeled "France," "The Middle East," and "South America."  Dulles holds a book with title: "How to Win Friends & Influence People by J.F.Dulles."  Dulles dominated American foreign policy during the Eisenhower administration, pressing other countries to join the United States in opposing communism at every opportunity.  While Britain and West Germany generally followed his lead, his bullying tactics were less successful in other countries and led to widespread criticism.  In 1953, while unsuccessfully pressing the French to join the European Defense Community, he threatened to conduct "an agonizing reappraisal" of American foreign policy, thereby alienating the French even further.  How to Win Friends and Influence People was the title of an immensely popular self-help book by Dale Carnegie.  Michael Cummings was a conservative cartoonist for the Daily Express for more than 40 years.

description: 1 drawing : ink brush, blue watercolor, and opaque white over graphite underdrawing ; 21.7 x 31.7 cm (sheet) | Editorial cartoon shows United States Secretary of State John Foster Dulles in front of a huge auditorium, divided into two sections, one labeled "Friends" and the other "Influenced People."  Only two sit on the Friends side:  German Chancellor Konrad Adenauer, dressed as a schoolboy labeled "Star Pupil," and British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan, shown as a poodle labeled "Old Faithful."  The Influenced People section is empty with overturned and broken chairs labeled "France," "The Middle East," and "South America."  Dulles holds a book with title: "How to Win Friends & Influence People by J.F.Dulles."  Dulles dominated American foreign policy during the Eisenhower administration, pressing other countries to join the United States in opposing communism at every opportunity.  While Britain and West Germany generally followed his lead, his bullying tactics were less successful in other countries and led to widespread criticism.  In 1953, while unsuccessfully pressing the French to join the European Defense Community, he threatened to conduct "an agonizing reappraisal" of American foreign policy, thereby alienating the French even further.  How to Win Friends and Influence People was the title of an immensely popular self-help book by Dale Carnegie.  Michael Cummings was a conservative cartoonist for the Daily Express for more than 40 years.

description: 1 drawing : ink brush, blue watercolor, and opaque white over graphite underdrawing ; 21.7 x 31.7 cm (sheet) | Editorial cartoon shows United States Secretary of State John Foster Dulles in front of a huge auditorium, divided into two sections, one labeled "Friends" and the other "Influenced People."  Only two sit on the Friends side:  German Chancellor Konrad Adenauer, dressed as a schoolboy labeled "Star Pupil," and British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan, shown as a poodle labeled "Old Faithful."  The Influenced People section is empty with overturned and broken chairs labeled "France," "The Middle East," and "South America."  Dulles holds a book with title: "How to Win Friends & Influence People by J.F.Dulles."  Dulles dominated American foreign policy during the Eisenhower administration, pressing other countries to join the United States in opposing communism at every opportunity.  While Britain and West Germany generally followed his lead, his bullying tactics were less successful in other countries and led to widespread criticism.  In 1953, while unsuccessfully pressing the French to join the European Defense Community, he threatened to conduct "an agonizing reappraisal" of American foreign policy, thereby alienating the French even further.  How to Win Friends and Influence People was the title of an immensely popular self-help book by Dale Carnegie.  Michael Cummings was a conservative cartoonist for the Daily Express for more than 40 years.
